grand_strategy.reading:
Chile under Kast is trying to turn its copper and lithium into a position it can hold between the United States and China, while it tightens the northern border as the proof that its security policy works. The balancing line is real but thin: the US coalition is joined with explicit limits, China is needed as a buyer, and the regional minerals pact with Argentina, Bolivia and Peru is the first sign that the neighbours can be partners on resources as well as on migration. The weak point is the border itself, whose results depend on the controls of Peru and Bolivia and on a Congress that has already rejected part of the plan.

The July 2026 surcharge shows the price of the first choice: the guarantor that Kast courted taxed about four tenths of his exports to it, spared the copper it needs, and asked for a rewrite of the free trade agreement and for rules against China, while the buyer took 43.7% of the copper and was received a day later. The same logic runs in the lithium (a state-led partnership inherited from Boric and kept by a government that wants private capital) and in the south (the courtesy to Milei on the Malvinas became a question about Magallanes and the Antarctic). Chile's real strategy is the width of its trade treaties (the US, the EU, Japan, Korea, Mercosur) and the metal itself; what it lacks is a way to make either great power pay for its choices.

stances.note: Kast calls the US relationship historic and strategic but says Chile is not allied with either superpower. Chile joined the Shield of the Americas, a US-promoted security coalition, and refused foreign troops on its soil and operations abroad. Warming is our reading of the coalition membership against the 2026 posture (C); the grade partner is our reading, since no source uses it and Kast's own word is that Chile is not aligned. Bond none is our reading. Update of 2026-10-16: the trend was warming until July 2026; the 12.5% US surcharge of that month (Section 301, about 40% of Chilean exports to the US, copper and lithium excluded) led the defence minister to say it raises doubts about the closeness and reliability of the relationship, and Washington asks for a rewrite of the 2004 FTA, so cooling is our reading (C) from those statements. The tie rests on the FTA in force since 1 January 2004 (USD 38.1bn of goods trade in 2025, USTR). Gap: the effect of the 2025 copper tariff on cathodes is not verified (sources conflict); the July 2026 surcharge excludes copper concentrates and cathodes.
